headline: Supported a proposed residential recycling collection policy and a direction for the annual borrowing proposal, both unanimously.
summary: Director Spencer said the proposed ordinance change would reduce truck traffic on residential streets. Commissioners asked about Champlain Parkway signal timing, crosswalk flashing lights, and a possible joint meeting on December 17, 2026. Staff also gave a report on the fall clean sweep and explained plans for an upcoming water plant tour.
decisions: Unanimously approved the consent agenda, which included the draft minutes of 9-16-26 and three ADA parking spaces.
Unanimously approved a motion to support the proposed residential recycling collection policy.
Unanimously approved a motion to support the proposed direction for the annual borrowing proposal and the concept of an inflationary adjuster, to be communicated to a committee and City Council.

decision_titles: Consent agenda: ADA parking spaces and draft minutes of 9-16-26
Proposed policy on residential recycling collection
Annual borrowing proposal and inflationary adjuster concept
plain_text:
DEPARTMENT OF PUBLIC WORKS 
645 PINE STREET 
BURLINGTON, VERMONT 05401 
COMMISSION MEETING NOVEMBER 38, 2026 
DRAFT MINUTES 
 
See video for full meeting – link below 
 
Commissioners Present:   Commissioner Benoit, Chair Damiani, Commissioner Davis; 
Commissioner Davis, Vice-Chair Fox; Commissioner Gallagher, Commissioner Hays; 
Commissioner O’Neil-Vivanco 
 
ITEM 1 – CALL TO ORDER 
Chair Damiani called the meeting to order at. 
ITEM 2 – AGENDA   
 Commissioner O’Neill-Vivanco made a motion to approve the agenda 
 Commissioner Gallagher seconded  
 Unanimous approval 
 
ITEM 3 – PUBLIC FORUM 
 Ali Hamedani requested bike racks in front of his business 
ITEM 4 – CONSENT AGENDA 
4.1 – Approval of Draft Minutes 9-16-26 
4.2  - Pomeroy Park ADA Parking Space 
4.3 -  30 Main St ADA Parking Space 
4.4 – 531 South Union St ADA Parking Space 
 
Commissioner O’Neill-Vivanco made a motion to approve consent agenda 
Commissioner Fox seconded 
Unanimous approval 
 
ITEM 5 –   PROPOSED POLICY ON RESIDENTIAL RECYCLING COLLECTION 
 
Director Spencer stated they were seeking an ordinance change that would put a policy 
in place that we believe would reduce truck traffic on residential streets and create a 
base for sustainable recycling. 
 
Commissioner Gallagher made a motion to support this program 
Commissioner O’Neill-Vivanco seconded 
Unanimous approval 
 
ITEM 6 –    PLANNING FOR UPCOMING WATER PLANT TOUR 
  
 Director Spencer and Division Director Moir explained the presentation.
ITEM 7 –   AUTHORIZED ANNUAL BORROWING PROPOSAL 
 
 Director Spencer 
Commissioner Fox made a motion to support approval for funding – the proposal 
direction 
 Commissioner O’Neill-Vivanco seconded the proposal direction 
Commissioner Davis stated he does not know if it needs to be amended or carry a 
second motion to see inflationary adjuster item as well support the concept of 
inflationary adjuster. 
 Commissioner Fox is friendly to an amendment 
 Commissioner O’Neill-Vivanco is a yes on the inflationary adjustment category 
Director Spencer stated it sounds like the motion is the support for the proposed 
direction that was laid out in the packet and support for the concept of inflationary 
adjuster as well to be communicated to the charger change Committee and City Council. 
 
Yes 
Unanimous approval 
 
ITEM 8 –   DIRECTOR’S REPORT 
   
Director Spencer gave a report on the fall clean sweep, which was very successful.  First 
full week of fall clean up.  
 
ITEM 9 -   COMMISSIONER ITEMS 
 
 Commissioner O’Neill-Vivanco attended the Route 127 safety audit  
  
Commissioner Hays inquired about the Champlain Parkway signal timing as there has 
been a back up on Austin Drive recently.  Commissioner Hays also asked about a 
signage, unsure of intersection, that says no merge or a yield sign. 
 
Commissioner Gallagher inquired about the pedestrian timing intervals 
Director Spencer stated the Walk/Bike Safety Action Plan did have a policy direction 
 
Commissioner Benoit also had a question about the Champlain Parkway stated bicyclist 
turning can press a button turning left there is no button to join traffic. 
 
Commissioner Fox asked if we had seen the petition going around about South Union 
Street, Also inquired about the North Champlain Street protected bike lane.  Director 
Spencer stated they are in contact with the fire department and the ability to serve 10 
North Champlain Street and what is needed for their apparatus. 
Commissioner Fox asked about the potential public meeting of combined commissions 
and the date proposed is December 17, 2026 which is the night after out meeting. 
Director Spencer stated that yes, the meeting is still happened and proposed we not 
meet on a regular meeting and have this special joint meeting and reconvene in January. 
 
Commissioner Davis asked about the flashing lights at the crosswalks.  Feels a warning 
sign should be added as drivers do not stop when the flashing light,
Also inquired about not allowing cars with studded snow tires in the parking garage. 
 
  
ITEM 10 – ADJOURNMENT AND NEXT MEETING DATE – DECEMBER 16, 2026a 
 
 Commissioner O’Neill-Vivanco made a motion to adjourn 
 Commissioner Fox seconded 
 Unanimous approval 
 
 Meeting adjourned at 8:18 p.m.
